transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Honestly, I’ve gotten so strict about cutting back how much I eat that I hardly feel like I’m taking in anything at all anymore. It's just become really hard for me to stop restricting myself.
Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating and consume an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?
No, I never lose control or eat large amounts of food like that. My focus is entirely on restricting what I take in, so I make sure I only eat very small, controlled amounts.
How do you feel about your body shape or weight, and does this influence how you see yourself?

I feel incredibly critical of my body, and every time I look in the mirror, all I can see is my stomach and thighs. It makes me feel like my appearance is the reason I was passed over for the promotion at work, and that I have to stay as small as possible to be worth anything.
Have you experienced a cessation of your menstrual periods for at least three consecutive months since you began this pattern of restrictive eating?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't kept close track of my periods lately with everything else going on.
In the last three months, have you engaged in any episodes of self-induced vomiting or the misuse of laxatives, diuretics, or enemas?
No, I don't do any of those things at all. I've never made myself throw up or used laxatives or anything like that. I only try to control my weight by strictly restricting how much food I eat.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent restriction of energy intake leading to a significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight, and a disturbance in the way her body weight or shape is experienced, while explicitly denying binge eating or purging behaviors, consistent with the restricting type of Anorexia Nervosa.
